purpose: Verified route seed for Garda Citizen Access. This site guides citizens to official processes and does not itself submit complaints, reports, applications or requests.
verification_note: Only routes with current official-source evidence are seeded here; conflicting or incomplete routes remain explicitly flagged.

routes.citizen_question: Emergency / immediate danger
routes.notes: 999 or 112; do not wait for an online form.
routes.purpose_plain: Get an immediate emergency Garda response.
routes.eligibility: Anyone who needs an emergency Garda response in Ireland.
routes.emergency_rule: Emergency route itself; do not wait for an online form.
routes.next_steps: Follow the emergency operator's instructions.
routes.guidance_basis: Official An Garda Síochána guidance/source linked in this route.
routes.conflict_note: No known source conflict recorded in this verification pass.

routes.citizen_question: I was directly affected by, or directly witnessed, Garda behaviour
routes.notes: Fiosrú determines admissibility; a Garda name is not required.
routes.purpose_plain: Make a formal complaint about Garda personnel through the statutory complaints system.
routes.eligibility: Initial screening asks whether the person was directly affected or directly witnessed the Garda behaviour; Fiosrú determines admissibility.
routes.deadline: Normally within 12 months; a late complaint may be considered where Fiosrú accepts there is good reason for the delay.
routes.next_steps: Fiosrú first assesses admissibility. An admissible complaint may be referred to An Garda Síochána for resolution under the statutory framework or investigated by Fiosrú, depending on the applicable route.
routes.conflict_note: Current page states Fiosrú is experiencing a high volume of complaints and possible admissibility delays. It also states complaint information may be shared with Gardaí and, in applicable circumstances, other bodies.
routes.legal_basis: Policing, Security and Community Safety Act 2024, Part 6, especially ss.195-199.
routes.guidance_basis: Official Fiosrú guidance/source linked in this route.

routes.citizen_question: I need to report a crime that does not fit a specialist online reporting route
routes.notes: Use a Garda station when no specialist online route fits.
routes.purpose_plain: Route general crime reports to the local Garda station or the appropriate official service after emergency and specialist screening.
routes.eligibility: Use when the matter falls within Garda jurisdiction and no more specific current online route is appropriate.
routes.emergency_rule: Emergency, danger to life, serious injury risk, crime in progress or offender at/near scene → 999/112.
routes.next_steps: Use the station directory or the specialist online service identified by the router.
routes.legal_basis: General criminal law and Garda statutory functions; route is operational guidance rather than a single offence-specific legal provision.
routes.guidance_basis: Official An Garda Síochána guidance/source linked in this route.
routes.conflict_note: No known source conflict recorded in this verification pass.

routes.citizen_question: I need to report a qualifying theft online
routes.notes: Current online theft declaration is for property not exceeding €1,000 in Ireland.
routes.purpose_plain: Submit the current online theft declaration where its conditions are met.
routes.eligibility: Current form is for theft of property not exceeding €1,000 in Ireland.
routes.emergency_rule: Do not use for emergencies or the categories excluded by Garda's online-reporting guidance.
routes.geographic_scope: Ireland excluding Northern Ireland for the current theft declaration
routes.next_steps: Provide the requested details; the current form warns that it cannot be edited after submission.
routes.legal_basis: Applicable Irish theft/criminal law and Garda online-reporting guidance.
routes.guidance_basis: Official An Garda Síochána guidance/source linked in this route.
routes.conflict_note: No known source conflict recorded in this verification pass.

routes.citizen_question: I want to report a non-emergency traffic incident
routes.notes: Current form says reports should generally be within 6 months.
routes.purpose_plain: Report a qualifying non-emergency road-traffic incident through Traffic Watch.
routes.eligibility: Current Traffic Watch conditions apply; the reporter must be willing to make a statement and attend court if required.
routes.emergency_rule: Emergency, serious injury collision or other urgent incident → 999/112.
routes.deadline: Current Traffic Watch form says reports should generally be made within 6 months.
routes.next_steps: Garda reviews the report; an investigator may contact the reporter and request a statement.
routes.legal_basis: Road Traffic Acts and current Garda Traffic Watch operational guidance.
routes.guidance_basis: Official An Garda Síochána guidance/source linked in this route.
routes.conflict_note: No known source conflict recorded in this verification pass.

routes.citizen_question: I experienced or witnessed a hate crime or hate-related incident
routes.notes: Emergency → 999/112.
routes.purpose_plain: Route hate crime and hate-related incident reports to the dedicated Garda service or local station.
routes.eligibility: Non-emergency suspected hate crime/hate incident.
routes.next_steps: A Garda will take the report and assess whether to commence an investigation; victim-support referral is available.
routes.legal_basis: Applicable Irish criminal law and current Garda hate-crime reporting guidance.
routes.guidance_basis: Official An Garda Síochána guidance/source linked in this route.
routes.conflict_note: No known source conflict recorded in this verification pass.

routes.citizen_question: I have information about crime or other activity and want to provide it confidentially
routes.notes: Garda Confidential: 1800 666 111.
routes.purpose_plain: Provide the dedicated confidential-information channel without confusing it with an ordinary crime report or Fiosrú complaint.
routes.eligibility: People wishing to provide relevant confidential information.
routes.next_steps: Provide information through the Garda Confidential Line. The Garda site states callers can provide crime-related information confidentially.
routes.legal_basis: Current Garda confidential-information service guidance.
routes.guidance_basis: Official An Garda Síochána guidance/source linked in this route.
routes.conflict_note: No known source conflict recorded in this verification pass.

routes.citizen_question: I want to access personal data Gardaí hold about me
routes.authority: An Garda Síochána Data Protection Unit
routes.notes: F20/data-protection access route; subject to applicable law.
routes.purpose_plain: Exercise the applicable data-protection access right using the Garda F20 route.
routes.eligibility: Subject to GDPR, Data Protection Act 2018 and applicable exemptions.
routes.next_steps: Garda Data Protection Unit processes the request subject to applicable law.
routes.legal_basis: GDPR and Data Protection Act 2018, subject to applicable exemptions.
routes.guidance_basis: Official An Garda Síochána Data Protection Unit guidance/source linked in this route.
routes.conflict_note: No known source conflict recorded in this verification pass.
routes.deadline: Current F20 guidance states Garda should respond within one month, with a possible extension of up to two further months for complex or numerous requests.
routes.evidence_required: Signed written request and acceptable proof of identity; additional authority/consent documentation may be needed for representative or third-party requests.
routes.review_or_appeal: If dissatisfied with the response or handling, the applicable data-protection complaint/rights route may include the Data Protection Commission; the specific response should be reviewed before selecting an escalation.

routes.citizen_question: I want records or administrative information from Gardaí
routes.notes: Current Garda sources describe response timing differently; preserve source-specific wording.
routes.purpose_plain: Route qualifying requests for Garda administrative records under FOI.
routes.eligibility: Subject to the Freedom of Information Act and exemptions; Garda identifies administrative areas including HR, Finance and Procurement.
routes.conflict_note: Current Garda pages/forms contain differing response-time wording; do not hard-code one universal deadline without qualification.
routes.next_steps: Check whether the information is within Garda's current FOI administrative scope and use the official application route.
routes.legal_basis: Freedom of Information Act 2014.
routes.guidance_basis: Official An Garda Síochána FOI Unit guidance/source linked in this route.

routes.citizen_question: I want environmental information held by Gardaí
routes.notes: AIE is distinct from FOI.
routes.purpose_plain: Route environmental-information requests under the separate AIE regime rather than ordinary FOI.
routes.eligibility: Subject to the AIE Regulations and applicable exceptions.
routes.next_steps: Describe the environmental information sought, provide contact details and state the preferred format.
routes.legal_basis: European Communities (Access to Information on the Environment) Regulations 2007–2018.
routes.guidance_basis: Official An Garda Síochána guidance/source linked in this route.
routes.conflict_note: No known source conflict recorded in this verification pass.

routes.citizen_question: I need a Garda Police Certificate
routes.notes: Specific current submission instructions must be verified before activation.
routes.purpose_plain: Route qualifying Police Certificate requests while keeping them separate from Garda Vetting.
routes.eligibility: Specified purposes include certain foreign consular/visa, EU, overseas employment/aid and qualifying overseas study circumstances.
routes.conflict_note: The same current Garda page says the application can be completed online, while its FAQ says to submit the completed application and certified documents by post. The site must preserve this conflict rather than assert a single submission method.
routes.next_steps: Check the qualifying purpose and current Garda submission instructions before sending the application.
routes.guidance_basis: An Garda Síochána, Data Protection / FOI / Police Certificates page, reviewed 2026-09-24.

routes.citizen_question: I need Garda vetting for work, volunteering or another organisation
routes.authority: An Garda Síochána National Vetting Bureau
routes.notes: Registered organisation initiates the application.
routes.purpose_plain: Explain that vetting is initiated through a registered organisation rather than as a standalone citizen application.
routes.eligibility: Generally for persons aged 16 or over through a registered organisation; additional consent requirements apply for ages 16–18.
routes.next_steps: Ask the organisation requesting vetting to initiate the eVetting process and provide the required identification/consent.
routes.legal_basis: National Vetting Bureau (Children and Vulnerable Persons) Act 2012 and current Garda vetting guidance.
routes.source_verified: Official Garda/National Vetting Bureau sources reviewed 2026-09-24
routes.guidance_basis: Official An Garda Síochána National Vetting Bureau guidance/source linked in this route.
routes.conflict_note: Current Garda pages show different headline turnaround figures (5-day/80% and 5–8 working days). The route uses the specific FAQ processing statement and avoids promising a fixed completion time.
routes.deadline: Current Garda guidance says completed applications are usually processed within 5–8 working days of receipt; the National Vetting Bureau notes that processing times can vary.
routes.evidence_required: Proof of identity is required; the registered organisation initiates the vetting process and the applicant completes the invitation/application steps.
routes.review_or_appeal: For application problems, contact the registered organisation's Liaison Person; applicants do not obtain Garda vetting forms directly from the National Vetting Bureau.

routes.citizen_question: I need an official Garda National Age Card
routes.notes: Voluntary proof-of-age card for people aged 18+.
routes.purpose_plain: Guide eligible applicants to the voluntary National Age Card process.
routes.eligibility: Available to persons aged 18 or over under the current scheme.
routes.next_steps: Complete the application through the official Age Card process and attend the relevant Garda station for authentication.
routes.legal_basis: Intoxicating Liquor Act 1988 (Age Card) Regulations 2007.
routes.guidance_basis: Official An Garda Síochána guidance/source linked in this route.
routes.conflict_note: No known source conflict recorded in this verification pass.

routes.citizen_question: I want to check whether property recovered by Gardaí may be mine
routes.notes: Search does not replace reporting stolen property.
routes.purpose_plain: Search the current Garda pilot database for selected unclaimed recovered property.
routes.eligibility: Public search of property included in the current pilot.
routes.geographic_scope: Selected participating locations/property covered by the current pilot
routes.next_steps: Search the official database. If the property was stolen, this does not replace reporting the theft.
routes.guidance_basis: Official An Garda Síochána guidance/source linked in this route.
routes.conflict_note: No known source conflict recorded in this verification pass.

routes.citizen_question: I received a Garda Fixed Charge Notice and want to understand payment or review/cancellation options
routes.authority: An Garda Síochána / Fixed Charge Processing System
routes.notes: Must not be presented as a new traffic report.
routes.purpose_plain: Separate payment, cancellation/review and information questions about Fixed Charge Notices.
routes.eligibility: Person who has received an FCN and meets applicable review/cancellation conditions.
routes.next_steps: Check the notice and use the official payment or cancellation/review route applicable to the specific notice.
routes.deadline: Normal payment structure is 56 days: first 28 days at the fixed amount, followed by a further 28 days at an increased amount, subject to the current notice/rules.
routes.conflict_note: Cancellation/review is a separate process and is not a guarantee that a notice will be cancelled.
routes.legal_basis: Road Traffic Acts and current Fixed Charge Notice regulations/guidance.
routes.guidance_basis: Official An Garda Síochána / Fixed Charge Processing System guidance/source linked in this route.

routes.citizen_question: I am a victim and want to understand or challenge a decision not to prosecute
routes.authority: An Garda Síochána / DPP depending on decision
routes.notes: Do not hard-code one universal deadline.
routes.purpose_plain: Identify whether the question concerns Garda prosecution decisions or a DPP review, without conflating the two.
routes.eligibility: Depends on the decision and applicable review route.
routes.conflict_note: Current Garda victim information and other official guidance contain differing review-period wording in different contexts; do not hard-code a single universal deadline.
routes.next_steps: Identify which authority made the decision and follow the corresponding official review information.
routes.guidance_basis: Official An Garda Síochána / DPP depending on decision guidance/source linked in this route.

routes.citizen_question: I need information about moving an abnormal or oversized load
routes.authority: An Garda Síochána / relevant local authority
routes.notes: Permit authority is the relevant local authority; Garda National Traffic Bureau has a notification/traffic-policing role.
routes.purpose_plain: Explain when an abnormal-load permit and Garda notification may be involved.
routes.eligibility: Depends on whether the proposed load falls within the current abnormal-load requirements.
routes.next_steps: Check the current local-authority permit requirements first; then follow the Garda notification requirements that apply to the load.
routes.deadline: For the Garda notification described in current guidance, a copy is to reach the Garda National Traffic Bureau at least 4 working days before submission to the local authority.
routes.legal_basis: Road Traffic and local-authority permitting framework; current Garda abnormal-load guidance.
routes.guidance_basis: Official An Garda Síochána / relevant local authority guidance/source linked in this route.
routes.conflict_note: No known source conflict recorded in this verification pass.

routes.citizen_question: I want to organise a public collection and need a collection permit
routes.notes: Use the current official collection-permit application route.
routes.purpose_plain: Route qualifying public collection permit applications to the official Garda process.
routes.eligibility: Subject to the applicable collection-permit requirements.
routes.next_steps: Use the current official collection-permit application and follow the responsible Garda instructions.
routes.legal_basis: Public Order/collection-permit legislation and current Garda collection-permit guidance.
routes.guidance_basis: Official An Garda Síochána guidance/source linked in this route.
routes.conflict_note: No known source conflict recorded in this verification pass.

routes.citizen_question: I want to run gaming or lotteries and need to know whether a Garda permit is required
routes.notes: Current GP1 is the specified application form; proposed activity date must meet the current lead-time requirement.
routes.purpose_plain: Screen gaming-permit questions and route qualifying applications to the current GP1 process.
routes.eligibility: Subject to the Gaming and Lotteries Act framework and current application requirements.
routes.next_steps: Check whether the proposed activity falls within the statutory licensing/permit regime and then use the official GP1 route.
routes.deadline: Current GP1 form states the proposed activity date should be at least 60 days from the application.
routes.legal_basis: Gaming and Lotteries Act 1956, as amended, including the 2019 amendments.
routes.guidance_basis: Official An Garda Síochána / District Superintendent guidance/source linked in this route.
routes.conflict_note: No known source conflict recorded in this verification pass.

routes.citizen_question: I want to apply for a firearm certificate
routes.notes: FCA1 is the current first-time application form; restricted firearms have the additional current authority requirement.
routes.purpose_plain: Route first-time firearm certificate applications to the official FCA1 process.
routes.eligibility: Eligibility and certificate conditions depend on the Firearms Acts and current Garda licensing requirements.
routes.next_steps: Use the current official FCA1 and submit through the responsible Garda licensing route.
routes.legal_basis: Firearms Acts 1925–2009 and current firearms licensing regulations/guidance.
routes.guidance_basis: Official An Garda Síochána guidance/source linked in this route.
routes.conflict_note: No known source conflict recorded in this verification pass.

routes.citizen_question: I need to renew a firearm certificate
routes.notes: Garda says the pre-populated FCR is the acceptable renewal route.
routes.purpose_plain: Route firearm-certificate renewals to the official renewal process.
routes.eligibility: Existing certificate holder with a renewal notice/current renewal process.
routes.next_steps: Use the current renewal instructions and pre-populated renewal documentation where applicable.
routes.legal_basis: Firearms Acts 1925–2009 and current firearms licensing regulations/guidance.
routes.guidance_basis: Official An Garda Síochána guidance/source linked in this route.
routes.conflict_note: No known source conflict recorded in this verification pass.

routes.citizen_question: I found property in a taxi or PSV / need the relevant property process
routes.notes: Specialist property process; use official instructions.
routes.purpose_plain: Use the current official route and instructions for this service.
routes.eligibility: See current official requirements.
routes.next_steps: Follow the current official instructions.
routes.guidance_basis: Official An Garda Síochána guidance/source linked in this route.
routes.conflict_note: No known source conflict recorded in this verification pass.

routes.citizen_question: I want to nominate a young person/group for a Garda Youth Award
routes.notes: Current awards include Individual, Group, Special Achievement and Community Safety nomination routes; age range is 13–21.
routes.purpose_plain: Use the current official route and instructions for this service.
routes.eligibility: See current official requirements.
routes.next_steps: Follow the current official instructions.
routes.guidance_basis: Official An Garda Síochána guidance/source linked in this route.
routes.conflict_note: No known source conflict recorded in this verification pass.

routes.citizen_question: I want to request public CCTV in my area
routes.authority: Relevant local authority / Garda institutional process
routes.notes: Do not present the published Section 28 form as a general citizen application; community proposals follow the relevant local-authority/community-safety pathway.
routes.purpose_plain: Explain that public CCTV proposals are handled through institutional/local-authority processes, not as an ordinary individual Garda application.
routes.eligibility: See current official requirements.
routes.next_steps: If the concern is a particular incident or existing footage, use the relevant crime/data/property route instead of treating this as a personal CCTV installation application.
routes.conflict_note: Do not present the institutional public-CCTV process as a standard citizen permit form.
routes.guidance_basis: Official Relevant local authority / Garda institutional process guidance/source linked in this route.

routes.citizen_question: Fiosrú has told me my complaint is inadmissible or that its investigation will be discontinued and I want a review.
routes.purpose_plain: Request the statutory review of an Fiosrú inadmissibility or discontinuance decision.
routes.eligibility: The original complainant; sufficient information must be provided to link the request to the original complaint.
routes.emergency_rule: This is a post-decision review, not an emergency route.
routes.contact: review@fiosru.ie; Review Unit, Fiosrú, 150 Upper Abbey Street, Dublin 1, D01 FT73
routes.deadline: Normally within 28 days of being informed of the decision; good reasons for additional time may be considered.
routes.next_steps: Fiosrú's independent review process considers whether the decision was fair, reasonable and proportionate on the available facts.
routes.conflict_note: Official Fiosrú review guidance provides a downloadable review form and confirms email/post submission. A separate discontinuance form is used where applicable; the website should select the form based on the decision received.
routes.legal_basis: Policing, Security and Community Safety Act 2024, s.224.
routes.guidance_basis: Official Fiosrú guidance/source linked in this route.
routes.review_or_appeal: Statutory review under section 224; normally request within 28 days of being informed of the inadmissibility decision, with good reasons for extra time considered.

routes.citizen_question: I am a victim of crime and need support or information
routes.purpose_plain: Connect victims with Garda Victim Service Offices and relevant support information.
routes.eligibility: Victims and people seeking information about Garda victim services.
routes.next_steps: Use Garda victim-service information and the relevant Victim Service Office.
routes.guidance_basis: Official An Garda Síochána guidance/source linked in this route.
routes.conflict_note: No known source conflict recorded in this verification pass.

routes.citizen_question: I want information about property held by Gardaí
routes.purpose_plain: Help distinguish property in Garda possession, recovered property and stolen-property reporting.
routes.eligibility: Depends on the type and circumstances of the property.
routes.next_steps: Identify whether the matter concerns property held by Gardaí, recovered property, or property reported stolen, then use the appropriate official route.
routes.guidance_basis: Official An Garda Síochána guidance/source linked in this route.
routes.conflict_note: No known source conflict recorded in this verification pass.

routes.citizen_question: I received a Fixed Charge Notice and need to understand or pay it
routes.purpose_plain: Understand current Fixed Charge Notice payment and related options.
routes.eligibility: Recipients of a Fixed Charge Notice.
routes.next_steps: Follow the instructions on the specific notice and current Garda FCN guidance.
routes.guidance_basis: Official An Garda Síochána guidance/source linked in this route.
routes.conflict_note: No known source conflict recorded in this verification pass.

routes.citizen_question: I made a GSOC complaint before Fiosrú began and need to know what happens now.
routes.purpose_plain: Understand the transition of a pre-2 April 2025 GSOC complaint to Fiosrú.
routes.eligibility: People with an existing GSOC complaint from before 2 April 2025.
routes.next_steps: No resubmission is required according to current Fiosrú guidance; Fiosrú will contact the complainant about next steps.
routes.guidance_basis: Official Fiosrú guidance/source linked in this route.
routes.conflict_note: No known source conflict recorded in this verification pass.

routes.citizen_question: I want to see, correct or understand personal information Gardaí hold about me
routes.authority: An Garda Síochána Data Protection Unit
routes.purpose_plain: Separate personal-data access/correction questions from FOI and environmental-information requests.
routes.eligibility: Depends on whether the request concerns the person's personal data, administrative records, environmental information, or another category.
routes.next_steps: Explain the data-right sought, then use the Garda Data Protection route and its current form/contact instructions.
routes.conflict_note: Do not present FOI as the route for a person's own personal-data access request when the Data Protection route applies.
routes.guidance_basis: Official An Garda Síochána Data Protection Unit guidance/source linked in this route.

routes.citizen_question: I cannot make a voice emergency call and need to contact emergency services by SMS
routes.purpose_plain: Explain the 112 SMS emergency option for deaf, hard-of-hearing or speech-impaired users.
routes.eligibility: For deaf, hard of hearing and speech-impaired users who need emergency assistance.
routes.emergency_rule: For qualifying emergencies only; SMS is not a real-time guaranteed service.
routes.next_steps: Use the official 112 SMS process and provide the requested location and emergency details.
routes.guidance_basis: Official Emergency services guidance/source linked in this route.
routes.conflict_note: No known source conflict recorded in this verification pass.

routes.citizen_question: I need Garda information or services in an accessible way
routes.purpose_plain: Help citizens identify accessibility support rather than forcing them through a standard digital route.
routes.eligibility: Anyone needing accessibility support to access Garda information or services.
routes.next_steps: Use the Garda accessibility information and request reasonable assistance where appropriate.
routes.guidance_basis: Official An Garda Síochána guidance/source linked in this route.
routes.conflict_note: No known source conflict recorded in this verification pass.

routes.citizen_question: I need help accessing or communicating with Fiosrú
routes.purpose_plain: Provide an accessible route to Fiosrú information and complaint processes.
routes.eligibility: Anyone who needs accessibility support when using Fiosrú services.
routes.next_steps: Use Fiosrú accessibility support or its Access Officer where assistance is needed.
routes.guidance_basis: Official Fiosrú guidance/source linked in this route.
routes.conflict_note: No known source conflict recorded in this verification pass.

routes.citizen_question: I live outside Ireland and need information about an Irish firearm certificate
routes.purpose_plain: Identify the separate route for non-resident firearm applicants instead of applying ordinary resident assumptions.
routes.eligibility: Non-resident applicants must satisfy the current statutory and Garda requirements.
routes.next_steps: Follow the current Garda non-resident licensing information and responsible authority instructions.
routes.legal_basis: Firearms Acts 1925–2009 and current firearms licensing regulations/guidance.
routes.guidance_basis: Official An Garda Síochána guidance/source linked in this route.
routes.conflict_note: No known source conflict recorded in this verification pass.

routes.citizen_question: I need proof of my criminal record status for another country or organisation
routes.purpose_plain: Help distinguish a Garda Police Certificate from Garda Vetting and other record-access routes.
routes.eligibility: Purpose determines whether a Police Certificate, Vetting or another route is appropriate.
routes.conflict_note: The same current Garda page says the application can be completed online, while its FAQ says to submit the completed application and certified documents by post. The site must preserve this conflict rather than assert a single submission method.
routes.next_steps: Identify the requesting organisation/country and purpose, then use the applicable official Garda route.
routes.guidance_basis: An Garda Síochána, Data Protection / FOI / Police Certificates page, reviewed 2026-09-24.

routes.citizen_question: I need to contact my local Garda station
routes.purpose_plain: Find the official station and local contact information without inventing local numbers.
routes.eligibility: Anyone needing a Garda station contact for a non-emergency matter.
routes.next_steps: Use the official station directory to identify the relevant station and its published contact details.
routes.guidance_basis: Official An Garda Síochána guidance/source linked in this route.
routes.conflict_note: No known source conflict recorded in this verification pass.

routes.citizen_question: I am involved in a Fiosrú investigation and want information about what is happening with the case
routes.purpose_plain: Request information about significant developments and decisions in a Fiosrú investigation.
routes.eligibility: Victims of crime involved in a Fiosrú investigation, subject to the applicable statutory framework.
routes.next_steps: Ask the Fiosrú investigating officer for the relevant information. If Fiosrú does not hold it, current guidance says the request can be forwarded to the appropriate organisation.
routes.legal_basis: Policing, Security and Community Safety Act 2024, Part 6; applicable victim-information provisions.
routes.guidance_basis: Official Fiosrú guidance/source linked in this route.
routes.conflict_note: No known source conflict recorded in this verification pass.
routes.review_or_appeal: If the requested information concerns a decision that can be reviewed, Fiosrú should explain the applicable review procedure; do not treat every information request as an appeal.

routes.citizen_question: Fiosrú finished investigating my complaint and I want to understand what happens next
routes.purpose_plain: Explain the possible outcomes after a Fiosrú investigation, including DPP or Garda Commissioner pathways and applicable review rights.
routes.eligibility: Complainants/victims whose Fiosrú investigation has reached an outcome.
routes.next_steps: Follow the outcome notification; if a discontinuance decision is received, use the statutory review route within the applicable period.
routes.legal_basis: Policing, Security and Community Safety Act 2024, Part 6.
routes.guidance_basis: Official Fiosrú guidance/source linked in this route.
routes.conflict_note: No known source conflict recorded in this verification pass.
routes.review_or_appeal: Outcome-specific. A closed investigation has no internal review facility according to the current Fiosrú Victims of Crime Charter; discontinuance has a statutory review route.

routes.citizen_question: Fiosrú discontinued its investigation and I want to request a review

routes.next_steps: Use the discontinuance-specific review form/process identified by Fiosrú.
routes.conflict_note: Official Fiosrú discontinuance review form verified 24 September 2026. Review normally requested within 28 days; good reasons may support extra time.
routes.legal_basis: Policing, Security and Community Safety Act 2024, s.224.
routes.guidance_basis: Official Fiosrú guidance/source linked in this route.
routes.review_or_appeal: Statutory review under section 224; normally request within 28 days of being informed of the discontinuance decision, with good reasons for extra time considered.

routes.citizen_question: I want to report a crime online, but I'm not sure whether the online form is suitable
routes.purpose_plain: Screen the incident before showing an online crime-reporting route.
routes.eligibility: Depends on incident type, location and current Garda online-reporting conditions.
routes.emergency_rule: Emergency, crime in progress, violent crime, burglary, stolen vehicle, stolen firearm or other excluded category → do not use the online declaration; use the appropriate Garda/emergency route.
routes.next_steps: Answer the incident-type and urgency questions, then use the appropriate official route.

routes.citizen_question: I want to complain about something a Garda did or failed to do
routes.purpose_plain: Screen the citizen's circumstances before sending them to the statutory Fiosrú complaint route.
routes.eligibility: Ask whether the person was directly affected, directly witnessed the behaviour, or is acting for someone under the applicable representative rules.
routes.emergency_rule: Immediate danger → 999/112; death/serious harm may engage separate statutory mechanisms and should not be pre-labelled by the website.
routes.deadline: Normally within 12 months, with statutory possibilities for extension.
routes.evidence_required: Useful details include Garda identity if known, dates/times/locations, description of behaviour and supporting information; a Garda name is not required.
routes.next_steps: If the citizen proceeds, direct them to the official Fiosrú complaint process. Fiosrú determines admissibility.
routes.conflict_note: The website must not promise admissibility or tell a person that a statutory threshold has definitely been met.
routes.legal_basis: Policing, Security and Community Safety Act 2024, ss.195-199 and s.226.
routes.guidance_basis: Official Fiosrú guidance/source linked in this route.
